newsitem.title: FINLAND: European integration vital for security -Ahtisaari.
newsitem.headline: European integration vital for security -Ahtisaari.

text.p: The success of European integration is vital for the security of the continent, Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari said on Wednesday.

"Failure with European integration would give us new economic and security policy hardships. The competitiveness of the European Union would deteriorate relative to growing economic areas," Ahtisaari told a seminar arranged by Finland's biggest industrial employer confederation.
"The base for social welfare states would weaken further. We would be forced to rebuild the foundation for the continent's security arrangement," he said.
Ahtisaari said Finland's recent European Parliament and local government elections indicated that many citizens were confused by the new situation after Finland joined the EU in 1995.
"Our economic problems are not, however, caused by the European Union nor by our preparations for the so called EMU discipline," he said.
Finland was influenced by the sweeping changes affecting all of Europe, Ahtisaari said.
One major factor behind the economic difficulties in Finland was the sudden disappearance of eastern trade when the former Soviet Union disintegrated in the early 1990s, he noted.
"Remaining outside, isolating ourselves, would have been troublesome, even fateful. As a member of the European Union we are a stronger guardian of our own interests," Ahtisaari said.

Finland has repeatedly expressed strong support for the planned third phase of Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), and for the 15-nation European Union's plans to expand to include the countries of the former Warsaw Pact.
